item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Nov 24, 2026
item.description: AI bubble: Stoic Finance: if the bubble pops the trillions poured into data centers and the jobs vanish with the index gains - a severe recession follows; Huang's saga only made that a few percent more likely, and Trump pressured the board to keep the bubble moving; Economist who called 2008 (via Owen Jones): market value is now more than twice GDP vs ~1.5x at the tech-bubble peak; a 30-50% fall cuts consumption ~2% of GDP, data-center construction falls with it, and the debt sits opaquely in private credit - 'we find out who's swimming naked'; Breaking Points: Huang's return doesn't solve the underlying problems - AI developers are finding it harder to raise debt and equity, neoclouds and the Anthropic IPO stay weak, and regulation is coming one way or the other. Supply/demand: Eli the Computer Guy: the oversupply evidence - dark GPUs, Amazon GPUs going straight to warehouses, ~600,000 GPUs sitting in Hong Kong, a TSMC surplus, and Colette Kress moving to shut the China gray channels that carry ~20% of actual lit-up sales; Bloomberg / MUFG: the pullback widens spreads and changes data-center financing pricing structurally, but GPU-financing demand is not going away - a secular, transformational trend with volatility and differentiation, not a cyclical event; Yahoo Finance panel: GPU and rental pricing keep rising while token pricing falls - an unsustainable model; some Nvidia margin pressure would actually help adoption and share, and the bulls' supercycle claim (Micron's president sees no stabilization point) meets the cycle skeptics; Yahoo Finance panel: one unnamed neocloud just had a massive contract canceled - trace the ripple through the whole supply chain when financing tightens; counterweight on Anthropic: the IPO was exceptionally successful, upsized into a bad macro backdrop, still above issue. Watchlist: Parkev Tatevosian: Nvidia at these prices and prospects is a great long-term deal, then into beaten-down Micron - now ~$700 after trading at $1,255; Parkev Tatevosian on TSMC: the best manufacturing company in the world, $356 after a $487 high against his $505 fair value - the primary manufacturer for Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom and Apple, so good that even Intel outsources to it; then ASML, the supplier to all of them; Tyler Hill on why AMD is making a lower low: the ~337M-share resale registration (~20.5% of shares out) is not AMD selling stock - it is mostly OpenAI and Meta warrants, up to 160M shares each, that vest only as they buy Instinct GPUs; CNBC / Jim Cramer defends Nvidia on circular financing: the bears say the deals sour, clients default and Nvidia drags the Nasdaq down, but the government is unlikely to stop them - and at 10x next year's earnings on ~75% sales growth the stock deserves 12x, about $199; Parkev Tatevosian: with backlog significant and shortages throughout the supply chain, Huang's return mitigates the disruption - two decades of trust with TSMC, the hyperscalers and the server makers that a new team could not replicate; Investing Tutorial: the bull case needs reassuring updates on supply, execution, margins and demand plus reduced regulatory uncertainty - set against the bear warning that Monday's rally may have been short covering, not lasting demand.

item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Nov 23, 2026
item.description: AI bubble: Sluker on why Huang's return doesn't end it - the circular-financing flywheel locks up when real corporations stop raising AI spend, and that is already happening; Eurodollar Talk on concentration - the whole economy leans on the AI trade, data-center spending growth has peaked, and the macro hit arrives the moment spending stops increasing; Akshat Shrivastava's counterweight - no earnings slowdown in the data, NVDA at a 0.15 PEG, a burst needs an earnings surprise; Pivot's Kara Swisher - shareholder value trumps every norm, enjoy the rally, its half-life is about 72 hours. Supply/demand: Market Signal on Jim Handy's memory warning - hyperscalers at ~40% of revenue in capex, memory margins could go from 80% to near zero in two quarters - and the counterweight: no slowdown in orders, supply won't catch demand before 2029, custom HBM isn't commodity memory, MU already ~4x forward; Motley Fool on Micron - $143B of FY27 free cash flow, LTAs to 2030-31 covering ~half of revenue. Watchlist: Schwab's Jay Woods on the reinstatement - down ~50% from the Oct 6 high, the SEC probe was the crescendo, 'I think we found the floor'; CBS on one CEO moving the whole market (NVDA +30%, Nasdaq +6%) and the Altman parallel; Kevin O'Leary gets the breaking news live on The Hill minutes after saying a return would never happen; Bloomberg on the governance overhaul that survives - compliance chief search, Harvey Jones stays chair; Motley Fool on Broadcom (~70% of custom AI chips, AI revenue +221%, supply secured to double to $115B in FY27) and on Intel, the contrary story (data-center & AI revenue +78%, server-CPU wafer reallocation, $200B TAM).

item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Nov 22, 2026
item.description: AI bubble: the Fed is popping it - Powell and Warsh blame the AI buildout for inflation, AI is now almost a third of corporate bond borrowing, and rate hikes hit everyone (Mo Bitar); the AI bill comes due and the chip king wobbles as Wall Street sells everything (Tech For Geeks); the counterweight - demand is real, Nvidia does about $1B a day in sales with ~$60B of quarterly profit, and a bubble is not the same as no lasting impact (OBF); Gareth Soloway - the bubble has already burst, a dot-com-style 70-80% decline still lies ahead, and Nvidia's P/E went from the mid-20s to 7 (David Lin). Supply/demand: cloud revenue growth is closing the spending gap fast, but power is now the binding constraint - Amazon has billions of dollars of Nvidia chips warehoused with nowhere to plug them in, voters revolted against data centers, and $2.5T vanished in a day (OBF); compute is so constrained Oracle can offer buyers extra options, GPU prices keep rising, HBM and DRAM are sold out through 2029, memory trades at 2-3x forward P/E and Nvidia at 7.5x (Jose Najarro); SpaceX and the supply of compute (Jo Bhakdi). Watchlist: Kyla Scanlon's Nvidia chapter from her Anthropic-IPO bubble breakdown; Parkev Tatevosian on the Reuters SEC-probe report - the worst week in Nvidia history, $2.5T lost since Oct 6 - and why the likely outcome is a fine and business as usual; Beat The Denominator - Nvidia at 0.15 EV/GP/RG is three times cheaper than Meta, Micron at under 3x forward EV/EBITDA with a 25% earnings yield, AMD and Broadcom still the expensive ones; the last time the regulators called (Finance Nerd); the 15-rules check on the chip crash - price is the one thing, and moves go higher and longer than you think (BacktoFundamentals).

item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Nov 21, 2026
item.description: AI bubble: can you call a bubble in real time? Shiller CAPE was near 1999-2000 levels, a 40% chance of a fall within three years (Bloomberg Podcasts/Justin Fox); follow the money - the AI trade cracked as money rotated out, then started leaving the market (TOS Indicators); Nasdaq fell 10% in a week, the worst correction since COVID, and the advice is don't panic (ITV News); Anthropic jumped 17% on its Nasdaq debut to a $1.8T cap, then fell 21% the next day (Eli the Computer Guy). Supply/demand: token volume up 35x year over year, agentic AI now 80% of tokens, GPU rental prices rising - Hopper re-contracted at twice the original price (Parkev Tatevosian on Nvidia's investor update); GPUs holding their value makes the financing of the buildout easier, since they're the collateral behind tens of billions in hyperscaler and neocloud debt (Parkev); the world stays compute constrained through 2028, hyperscalers are supply constrained and building into contracted demand, not on hope (FinVid). Watchlist: AMD at $424 vs Nvidia at $125 - margins of 18 vs 66 per $100 of sales, Nvidia at 8.6x forward earnings with a $262 intrinsic value (Dividend Talks); Micron stress test - cut memory cash flow in half and the stock still has 18% downside at $594 (Dividend Talks); Nvidia post-Huang: pipeline set to 2029, 9.8x forward P/E with 75% revenue growth forecast, $259 fair value vs ~$150 (Parkev); the board - Nvidia, Broadcom and ServiceNow stay strong buys, Sandisk joins, Micron, SK Hynix and TSMC stay buys (Dividend Talks).

item.description: AI bubble: Breaking Points on the compute-first model dying as banks pull back from data-center lending; ETFcom on breadth as the AI wave crashing ashore and a possible lost decade; Hence Documentary on Anthropic's IPO, bulls vs bears; Jo Bhakdi on whether the market is cheap or a bubble. Supply/demand: Gene Munster on why the AI buildout could still drive tech higher; Parkev on Micron sold out through 2027-28 with memory prices up 200-300% and agentic AI lifting Intel CPU demand; ETFcom on capex heading to $1.2T next year with demand still outstripping supply and GPU rents rising. item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Nov 19, 2026
item.description: AI bubble: Global News on the bubble debate — AI stocks drove 50-75% of S&P 500 gains and ~40% of US GDP growth, and the Anthropic IPO is the bellwether; MonkeyExplains on Anthropic's numbers — $16.3B H1 revenue (14x) against an $80.7B loss and a $1.4T valuation; Stoic Finance on the IPO terms — $107.3B raised, $1.5T value, a $26B private placement from Nvidia/Google/AMD, and the $2T target missed; Stoic on the coming share-supply flood — +2,000% over the next year, with SpaceX down 30% post-IPO as the warning; Geopolitical Economy Report on AI's $4.9T revenue gap and a report finding no AI benefits outside tech. Supply/demand: Geopolitical Economy Report on the neocloud crisis and CoreWeave's debt risk; Couch Investor on Anthropic's economics — revenue ramping toward $270B by fiscal 2028, gigawatt commitments, and falling token prices pressuring compute pricing; Parkev on the cloud backlog — +$500B in three months to $2.5T, with data-center readiness, power and land the binding constraints; Verified Investing on the IPO as market barometer — the pre-IPO selloff was capital-raising for the $90B+ offering. Watchlist: Couch Investor on Nvidia — seven straight down weeks and weekly RSI at its lowest since the October 2022 bottom; Parkev doubling down on Broadcom — 55% EPS growth, AI revenue doubling toward $230B, 48.6% margins, a forward P/E of 9.6 and a $451 DCF value vs $333; Dan Ives on his $225 Nvidia target and the fight over Jensen's return; AMD's seat in the AI gold rush and Google's new opening; MarketBeat on the numbers behind the Anthropic IPO.

item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Nov 16, 2026
item.description: AI bubble: Steven Van Metre - Blackstone's datacenter giant QTS went looking for $800M and came back with $300M, lenders walking away from the best credit in the business; The Young Turks - Elon Musk admits the AI datacenter buildout is a giant bubble, debt markets have shut off the neoclouds and 'guppy level death' is coming; Capital Insight - Ed Dowd says AI was 45% of the market, the tech bubble has already burst, and Nvidia will miss within six months as hyperscalers go negative free cash flow; Neal K. Shah - Nvidia's circular financing machine and over $530B in shadow liabilities; RedGamingTech - the Commerce Department's new remote-access chip rules, SemiAnalysis cutting AI accelerator capex 20-40% through 2030, and Goldman desk confidence fading. Supply/demand: Steven Van Metre - the credit cycle is turning, buyers are full, banks are stuck holding loans, and BofA says deals are being pushed to 2027; The Young Turks - even Jensen Huang admits there isn't enough capital for the neoclouds, CoreWeave down 41% with distressed bonds; Verified Investing - the week ahead: Warsh, Nvidia earnings, and the Anthropic IPO. Pricing: RedGamingTech - RTX 5090s around $6,500, still 3x MSRP, but used prices down 20-30% and availability improving. Watchlist: Finance Deep Dive - Dan Ives is still buying Nvidia, on Colette Kress and the CEO candidates; Verified Investing - Nvidia ahead of earnings; Joe Blogs - the sell-off spreading across Asia with TSMC down 5.7% and Nvidia down $1.9T from its October peak; Joe Blogs - Nvidia's earnings preview, $108-109B expected with zero China revenue assumed, and CoreWeave's $709M quarterly loss on $846M of interest; Meet Kevin - the SemiAnalysis bear case, a $1.6T spending cut, and why it's a delay, not a cancellation.

item.description: AI bubble: Meerkat Explains - the market can't decide if the bubble popped, CoreWeave is paying 16% to borrow with lenders pricing a coin-flip chance it repays, and the whole tower rests on a chipmaker's promise to rent the chips itself; Meerkat - a bubble is a price kept alive by darkness, the AI giants were funded by a sealed private room passing the parcel at ever-higher prices while the labs lose $1.60 per dollar of revenue; Meerkat - Burry has reportedly bet against the biggest names, the Mag 7 are worth $24T and a third of the average 401(k) sits in them, and the takeaway is the bubble hasn't failed to pop, it has failed to be looked at; The Bigger Board - a day-by-day scenario of the bubble bursting tomorrow, from the trigger to the stock market's first day. item.description: AI bubble: Finance Stack - nearly one in five Korean adults own Samsung, the market has lost nearly half its value, and AI is now a fifth to a third of US growth with the Mag 7 a third of the S&P; Finance Stack - the other side: hyperscalers can afford their debts, the IMF's AI crash scenario is a 2000-size problem not 2008, but SoftBank and Thiel sold all their Nvidia and Burry is short; TheOneLanceB - the correction is hot but not irrationally exuberant, and the Anthropic IPO needs a mildly more cautious stance. item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Nov 12, 2026
item.description: AI bubble: Ed Zitron - Nvidia was the bank of AI, and with Huang gone the circular financing that propped up the ecosystem is over (The Tech Report); Paul's Hardware - is the bubble bursting? Trust no one selling a certain answer, and if AI hits a wall, data-center demand falls off hard; TheTechnicalTraders - Nvidia down 11% today, 36% from the highs, and Anthropic's ~$90B IPO looks like a feeding frenzy. Supply/demand: Innovation Uncovered - hyperscalers spent ~$200B on capex in Q3, Meta's free cash flow went negative and buybacks hit the lowest since 2017, so the buildout is now debt-funded; Nick Saraev - OpenAI runs ~100% on Nvidia while Anthropic is only ~33% and is building custom silicon, shifting the compute balance; NBC DFW - Georgia's data centers will double state power demand in five years, and the fight is over who pays for the grid. Watchlist: CBS - the timeline of Huang's resignation, from the affair admissions to the board's move; Schwab/Jablonski - were investors buying Nvidia or Jensen Huang? Demand for compute is intact and a lot of AI stocks are on sale; Schwab/Hanks - the facts: $5.7T to $4.2T market cap, Ives' $225 target without Huang, AMD +23% and Broadcom +17% this week; Tom Lee on CNBC - watch talent retention, the thing that would tell you if Nvidia is weathering this.

item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Nov 11, 2026
item.description: AI bubble: The Tech Report panel asks 'is AI in a bubble?' - value accrues to chipmakers, frontier models face a pricing equilibrium, like the web in 2001; Ed Dowd - the tech bubble has already burst, semis are in a bear market, Nvidia to miss as hyperscalers turn free-cash-flow negative (CapitalCosm); Sabine Hossenfelder - the AI boom is financed on borrowed money, $466B in nine months, and the key test is getting users to subscribe. Supply/demand: CoreWeave's earnings sparked the rally - revenue beat, backlog jumped to $132.5B, cheaper contract-backed financing at 7-7.5% plus $9B in customer prepayments (The Hostile Takeover); WSJ - midterm voters pushed back on data centers, and Texas, Ohio and Georgia hold ~40% of US capacity; George Packer - the backlash could crash a stock market held up by AI, while wage earners see little benefit (Amanpour and Company). Watchlist: CBS - Nvidia's board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang; NBC4 - the scandal in brief: stock down 4% Monday, ~$190B wiped out, board investigation and shareholder lawsuit; Parkev Tatevosian - Dan Ives puts 25-30% downside on Nvidia if Huang goes, yet Nvidia trades at a forward P/E of 10.5, cheapest in years; Tyler Hill - the premarket rally recap and the levels that matter (AMD above 580, Micron above $829), CoreWeave's report saved the sector; The Hostile Takeover - rally breadth: SMH +5.7%, Micron +13%, Marvell +10%, Nvidia +3.9%, Applied Materials +7%, AMD +8.9%, Broadcom +5.3% - bottoms form on bad news.
